title: M5Unified #446 follow-up: merged develop PCF8563 timer preservation

hardware.reason: No CoreInk or other PCF8563 board is available locally or through the Device Service; only the dial (M5Dial) virtual profile provides a PCF8563 model.

execution.environment: macOS arm64; local ESP-IDF v6.0.2; Device Service dial profile (M5Dial, QEMU, PCF8563 register model)

checks.detail: Merged develop (dae3b5d) built with pinned local M5Unified/M5GFX; merged BIN 503424 bytes.
M5Dial QEMU session booted the sketch and returned PCF8563 register readbacks (0x0E/0x01/0x0F) over I2C.
disable_rtc_irq=false kept 0x82 across M5.begin(), clearIRQ() and a later Rtc.begin(); setTimerIRQ(0)/disableIRQ() left 0x03; the default path left 0x03.
Timer countdown, TF latching and INT firing are not observable: the QEMU PCF8563 model has no countdown logic (0x0F does not decrement).
No PCF8563 physical board or CoreInk virtual profile available.
Power-off to RTC wake repetition, including M5.Power.timerSleep(seconds), was not executed.

notes: Merged commit dae3b5d has the same tree as the previously reviewed PR head 4a0ebfd (git diff --stat empty; compare API files=[]).
Issue #446 is Japanese; the reply is Japanese. One comment only.
Issue remains OPEN; no close, approval, push or upstream change.
QEMU model limit: only time registers 0x02-0x08; CNT (0x0F) is stored but does not count down.
Reply posted once: issuecomment-7061225804; issue remains OPEN.
